sonnet.problem: The card gives the first words of Psalm 22:21 ('at the horns of the wild oxen') and asks the baker to supply what God has done. Story card 3 cuts the verse off before 'You have answered me,' so the baker has nothing to reason from. This is guessing the next words of a line.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

sonnet.problem: The card says David is 'poured out like water' and asks what his heart is like. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason their way to 'wax.' Stone and fire are equally believable, so the baker is guessing a picture's wording, like the 'anoint with oil, myrrh or perfume' example.
sonnet.rule: Prep must never become a guessing game. ... The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
